column3: NASB renders “are gathered together to Him” as “gathered around Him” and adds “when.”
NASB follows the critical text without “they found fault”; “defiled” is rendered “impure.”
NASB opens a parenthesis (to v. 4) and renders “with a fist” as “carefully.”
NASB has no “and couches,” though the packet’s critical text includes it; “vessels” and “utensils” are rendered “pitchers and copper pots.”
NASB follows the critical text (“impure hands”).
NASB has no “answering,” like the critical text; the quotation is in capitals.
NASB adds “but”; the quotation is in capitals.
NASB follows the critical text without the Textus Receptus list of washings.
“Neatly” is rendered “You are experts at.”
Close to the Greek; the quotations are in capitals.
NASB puts the explanation of “Corban” in parentheses as “given to God.”
Close to the Greek.
“Making void” is rendered “invalidating.”
NASB follows the critical text (“again”) and adds “of you.”
NASB follows the critical text (“out of the man”) and adds “if.”
This verse is absent from the critical text; NASB prints it in braces, following the Textus Receptus.
NASB follows the critical text with “the parable.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text (“purifying”) and renders it as a parenthetical comment: “Thus He declared all foods clean.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB moves “adulteries” from v. 22 into this verse; “sexual immorality” is rendered “fornications.”
NASB renders “an evil eye” as “envy” and “covetous desires” as “deeds of coveting.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text with “Tyre” only; “He was not able to be hidden” is “He could not escape notice.”
NASB follows the critical text (“immediately”).
“Was asking” is rendered “kept asking.”
NASB follows the critical text (“He was saying”).
NASB has “Yes,” a Textus Receptus word.
“Word” is rendered “answer.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the child lying on the bed”).
